preview: An interview experience at Amazon for a summer internship consisting of an online coding and MCQ round followed by two technical rounds focused on data structures and algorithms.
content:
Amazon interview experience

Round 1 : Coding + Technical Mcqs

The Test was hosted on Hackerearth platform. It consisted of 20 Mcqs consisting of Ds, Algo, Os, Dbms and Networking. They were of 1 mark each.
There were 2 coding questions which were pretty simple and can be solved by Brute force approach. They were of 40 marks each.
Question links:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/count-total-number-digits-1-n​/
https://www.codechef.com/SNCKPB17/problems/SNELECT

Round 2 : Technical Round 1 (21 were shortlisted)

The interview started with discussion on resume projects. Then he started with a question on tree.

a) Given two binary trees. We need to merge them into a new binary tree. The merge rule is that if two nodes overlap, then sum node values up as the new value of the merged node. Otherwise, the non-null node will be used as the node of new tree (structure may and may not be same of both binary trees).
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/merge-two-binary-trees-node-sum​/

b) Given two numbers represented by two linked lists, write a function that returns sum list. The sum list is linked list representation of addition of two input numbers. It is not allowed to modify the lists. Also, not allowed to use explicit extra space (Hint: Use Recursion).
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sum-of-two-linked-lists​/
The interviewer had asked me to write whole code on paper with proper syntax and he would also test it thoroughly.

Round 3 : Technical Round 2 (Then there were 7)
This round started with discussion of what all questions asked in previous interview round. And then he started with coding questions.

a) Given an array and a number k where k is smaller than size of array, we need to find the k’th smallest element in the given array. He told me to write the entire code on paper.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/kth-smallestlargest-element-unsorted-array​/

b) You have an input stream of numbers and asked to make groups of consecutive numbers and output how may groups of numbers can be formed. He asked me to give a approach of how would I solve it. I gave a solution using a list of set.
Eg
Input stream 2 6 1 4 5
So after 2
[{2}]                  o/p = 1
After 6
[{2},{6}]            o/p = 2
After 1
[{1-2},{6}]        o/p = 2
After 4
[{1-2},{4},{6}]  o/p = 3
After 5
[{1-2},{4-6}]    o/p = 2

Later he asked me about my resume and what I do in free time.

5 were selected for summer internship

Tips for preparation :
Amazon mostly focuses on DS and algo so i would advice to go through all the interview experience on geeks for geeks and find the patterns of what amazon usually ask in interviews.
Basic knowledge about OS,  networking and dbms should be known as they could also ask it.
